title: University of Illinois Extension: When Should I Start Cleaning My Garden?
note: In the Midwest, mid-April is the earliest to clean up, ideally when temperatures are reliably in the 50s °F; leave 8 to 24 in of stalk for nesting bees.

title: Iowa State Extension: Spring Garden Tasks
note: Wait until temperatures are consistently around 50°F before removing spent plant material; remove winter mulch in stages; divide perennials as they emerge; never work wet soil.

title: Iowa State Extension: How Should I Prepare My Perennial Beds for Winter?
note: Cut back after a hard freeze; add about 4 in of mulch once the ground freezes (late November); mulching earlier can delay dormancy.

title: Iowa State Extension: How Do I Care for Ornamental Grasses?
note: Cut back ornamental grasses in early spring before new growth appears.

title: Rutgers NJAES: Landscape Plants Rated by Deer Resistance
note: Rates plants A (rarely damaged), B (seldom severely damaged), C (occasionally severely damaged) or D (frequently severely damaged). Plants rated C or D get the antler icon. Rated at genus level where Rutgers lists a whole genus. Plants Rutgers does not list are left unrated.
